## Solution

**Setup and key equivalence.** For an infinite product $\prod c_n$ with positive factors, convergence (to a nonzero finite limit) is equivalent to convergence of the series $\sum \log c_n$. This is because the partial products $P_N = \prod_{n=1}^N c_n$ satisfy $\log P_N = \sum_{n=1}^N \log c_n$, and $\log$ is a continuous bijection between $(0,\infty)$ and $\mathbb{R}$.

Since $\prod a_n$ and $\prod b_n$ both converge (with positive factors), the series
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \log a_n \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{n=1}^\infty \log b_n$$
both converge. In particular, $\log a_n \to 0$ and $\log b_n \to 0$, so $a_n \to 1$ and $b_n \to 1$.

---

**(a) $\prod (a_n + b_n)$ — DIVERGES.**

Since $a_n \to 1$ and $b_n \to 1$, we have $a_n + b_n \to 2$. Therefore
$$\log(a_n + b_n) \to \log 2 \neq 0.$$
The general term of the series $\sum \log(a_n + b_n)$ does not tend to zero, so the series diverges. Hence $\prod(a_n + b_n)$ **diverges**. More precisely, for sufficiently large $n$, $a_n + b_n > 1$ (e.g. $> 3/2$), so the partial products tend to $+\infty$.

---

**(b) $\prod a_n^2$ — CONVERGES.**

We have
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \log(a_n^2) = 2\sum_{n=1}^\infty \log a_n,$$
which converges since $\sum \log a_n$ converges. Therefore $\prod a_n^2$ **converges**, with value
$$\prod_{n=1}^\infty a_n^2 = \left(\prod_{n=1}^\infty a_n\right)^2.$$

---

**(c) $\prod a_n b_n$ — CONVERGES.**

We have
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \log(a_n b_n) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \log a_n + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \log b_n,$$
which converges as the sum of two convergent series. Therefore $\prod a_n b_n$ **converges**, with value
$$\prod_{n=1}^\infty a_n b_n = \left(\prod_{n=1}^\infty a_n\right)\left(\prod_{n=1}^\infty b_n\right).$$

---

**(d) $\prod \frac{a_n}{b_n}$ — CONVERGES.**

We have
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \log\frac{a_n}{b_n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \log a_n - \sum_{n=1}^\infty \log b_n,$$
which converges as the difference of two convergent series. Therefore $\prod \frac{a_n}{b_n}$ **converges**, with value
$$\prod_{n=1}^\infty \frac{a_n}{b_n} = \frac{\prod_{n=1}^\infty a_n}{\prod_{n=1}^\infty b_n}.$$

---

**Summary:**

| Part | Product | Convergence |
|------|---------|-------------|
| (a) | $\prod(a_n + b_n)$ | Diverges (to $+\infty$) |
| (b) | $\prod a_n^2$ | Converges; equals $\left(\prod a_n\right)^2$ |
| (c) | $\prod a_n b_n$ | Converges; equals $\left(\prod a_n\right)\left(\prod b_n\right)$ |
| (d) | $\prod \frac{a_n}{b_n}$ | Converges; equals $\frac{\prod a_n}{\prod b_n}$ |
